scope: stdlib static finite counterexamples; not native model/data execution

physical-scene-state-interchange.finding: Correct same-target exchange predictions and harmful different-target controls do not identify recipient-language use. Donor states may encode target identity. This disproves a sufficient identification claim, not possible training benefit.

same-target-description-grounding.finding: Target-equivalent outputs do not imply equal latent scene representations. Nuisance description information can coexist with correct grounding. Same-target identity alone does not specify which hidden dimensions should be invariant.

same-forward-coverage-diagnosis.finding: Covered outcomes and observational agreement cannot identify whether language or visual state determines a prediction. This is a logical counterexample, not a fitted explanation for the captured TRAIN failures; known head-architecture confounding remains.

limitations: No new native forward, backward, AMP, resource, VAL or training claim.
Finite lookup construction demonstrates non-identification; it does not assert the actual network uses this shortcut.
No universal pretrained hard-IoU improvement admission requirement.
No new mechanism or prior-art novelty demonstrated.
